Compositing involves `MPI_Alltoallv` communication, which is reduced in hybrid mode by aggregating messages per socket [S2].

The evidence explicitly states that the compositing stage uses an 'MPI Alltoallv call' for communication. It further explains that in hybrid implementations, 'only one thread per socket participates in the compositing phase,' and this thread 'gathers fragments from all other threads in the same socket, packs them into a single buffer, and transmits them.' This process of gathering and packing fragments from multiple threads into a single buffer per socket before transmission constitutes aggregating messages per socket, which reduces the total number of messages compared to every thread sending individually.

Hybrid Parallel Volume Rendering is a parallel programming model that combines distributed-memory parallelism (MPI) for inter-node communication with shared-memory parallelism (threads/GPU) for intra-node computation [S1, S2].

The claim states that Hybrid Parallel Volume Rendering combines distributed-memory parallelism (MPI) for inter-node communication with shared-memory parallelism (threads/GPU) for intra-node computation. Source [S1] explicitly states: 'Hybrid parallelism provides the best of both worlds: using distributed-memory parallelism across a large numbers of nodes increases available FLOPs and memory, while exploiting shared-memory parallelism among the cores within each node ensures that each node performs its portion of the larger calculation as efficiently as possible.' It further details that the implementation uses MPI for distributed tasks and shared-memory techniques like POSIX threads, OpenMP, or CUDA (GPU) for intra-node parallelism. Source [S2] corroborates this by describing the use of MPI for distributing data across PEs and pthreads/OpenMP for shared-memory parallelism within those PEs. All facts in the claim are present in the evidence.
